en.name: Zephyrinus
en.summary: A pope who navigated early disputes over how to describe the relationship between God the Father and Christ the Son.
en.body: Zephyrinus's reign was marked by growing theological controversy over Modalism, a teaching that described the Father and the Son as different modes of a single divine person rather than distinct persons — a position the church would ultimately reject as it developed Trinitarian doctrine. His chief adviser and later successor, Callixtus, played a significant role in these disputes, which also drew the strong disapproval of the theologian Hippolytus, who would later become a rival claimant to the papacy.
